style_when: the article describes one decisive moment or place — a yard at dawn, a control room, a shutdown line, a handover — that a film still could hold
prompt: Cinematic split-screen diptych inside a residential garage. Left half: an ageing gas push mower parked on cracked concrete, a plastic fuel jerry can and a small oil bottle standing beside its deck, rust and ochre stains below. Right half: a clean cordless mower in bone-white housing, its battery pack docked in a charger with one green status light. Divided by a clean vertical seam of painted wood, both halves sharing the same concrete floor. 35mm anamorphic look, shallow depth of field, cool blue-hour light spilling from the open garage door behind, a warm amber worklight raking from the left, graphite, rust and bone-white palette, fine film grain, no people.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, watermarks, logos
rationale: This is the catalogue's literal gas-versus-electric duality, so the frame is a split-screen diptych inside the garage where the 90-day fuel clock actually runs. Cinematic_still supplies the decisive storage moment — blue-hour light through the open door, one warm worklight — so the jerry can and oil bottle read as the written upkeep tax the cordless side simply omits.
cue: The fuel aged on a clock nobody saw
subject: a gas push mower beside a fuel jerry can and oil bottle, split against a cordless mower docked on its battery charger
core_thesis: A gas mower's upkeep is written by its engine maker — oil after the first 5 hours, then every 50 hours or yearly, and fuel drained inside a 90-day window — while a cordless mower that cuts a quarter acre inside one 45–50-minute charge replaces that entire written schedule with nothing.
core_conflict: The gas engine's hidden upkeep tax — a maker-mandated oil, plug and fuel-rotation schedule running on a 90-day storage clock — against the cordless mower's single charge-run ceiling, where the whole service list simply disappears.
composition: Split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast — the gas mower with its fuel-and-oil service artifacts on the left, the cordless mower on its charger on the right, divided by a clean vertical seam
alt_text: A gas push mower beside a jerry can and oil bottle, split against a cordless mower on its charger in a garage.
caption: The engine maker writes the gas mower's service list; the cordless half of the garage keeps only a charger.
title: Gas mower with fuel can versus cordless mower on charger, garage split-screen
